mechanism: "blocksdir" is a DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS row (src/config-options.lisp:437), so it is accepted, warned about once, and never read. The block store has no second base: BLOCK-STORE has one BASE-PATH slot (src/storage/blocks.lisp:44), INIT-BLOCK-STORE is called from exactly one site with the node's data directory (src/node/init.lisp:596 -> src/storage/blocks.lisp:592-594), and every path is a literal merge against it -- ENSURE-DIRECTORIES merges "blocks/" (:77-79), BLOCK-FILE-PATH merges "blocks/<hash>.blk" (:85-87), the blk and rev FLAT-FILE-SEQs are built from ENSURE-DIRECTORIES' result (:106-111, :206-211), and INIT-BLOCK-STORE derives the xor.dat directory by merging "blocks/" against the same BASE-PATH a second time (:592-613). The declared *BLOCKS-DIRECTORY* at :11 has no SETF site anywhere in src/ or tests/ (grep). Core at d3056bc splits the two: ArgsManager::GetBlocksDirPath() (common/args.cpp:286-309) returns fs::absolute(GetPathArg("-blocksdir")) / <chain subdir> / "blocks" when -blocksdir is set and GetDataDirBase()/<chain subdir>/"blocks" otherwise, and that path becomes BlockManager's m_opts.blocks_dir (init.cpp:1137, :1339), which is what the blk and rev FlatFileSeqs, the xor.dat key and the CheckDiskSpace call use (node/blockstorage.cpp:1191, :1228-1229, validation.cpp:2775). Note that the finding's core_ref overstates one detail: Core keeps blocks/index in the DATADIR (init.cpp:1140, :1342 -- args.GetDataDirNet() / "blocks" / "index"), so only the blk/rev/xor bulk moves; that does not change the mechanism. Core also refuses to start when the named directory is missing: init.cpp:968-970, InitError("Specified blocks directory \"%s\" does not exist."), which fires because GetBlocksDirPath() returns an empty path when -blocksdir is not a directory (common/args.cpp:295-300).
consequence: The deployment -blocksdir exists for -- a small fast volume for the datadir and chainstate plus a large disk for block data -- silently does not happen: every blk/rev byte lands on the datadir volume. On mainnet that is hundreds of GB onto a disk sized for the chainstate, and the terminal state is ENOSPC in the middle of a block write, the case our storage layer recovers from least cleanly. A missing -blocksdir target is also not fatal here, so an unmounted volume presents as a node that quietly writes to the mount point's underlying disk instead of refusing to start. The dimension-wide mitigation does apply and is real: the WARN naming -blocksdir is the FIRST line of debug.log and reaches the console, so this is announced rather than silent. It stays S2 rather than S3 because the consequence is not the absence of an extra check but an active, unbounded write to a volume the operator explicitly directed the node away from, and the warning does not stop that volume filling days later.

fix_shape: Give the block store the second base path Core gives BlockManager, rather than a global. Add a BLOCKS-PATH slot to BLOCK-STORE alongside BASE-PATH and have INIT-BLOCK-STORE take it as an argument, defaulting to (merge-pathnames "blocks/" base-path); compute it once at startup with Core's rule -- when -blocksdir is set, (fs::absolute blocksdir) / <network subdirectory> / "blocks", else the datadir form -- and thread it through the three constructors that currently derive a path from BASE-PATH (ENSURE-DIRECTORIES, BLOCK-FILE-PATH, and the blk/rev FLAT-FILE-SEQ plus the xor.dat key reader). Keep blocks/index and the undo directory where they are: Core's block index LevelDB stays under GetDataDirNet()/blocks/index (init.cpp:1140), so only blk/rev/xor move, and moving the index too would make a Core datadir unreadable. Turn "blocksdir" into a real DEFINE-OPTION row with a start-node keyword, and add Core's pre-flight refusal -- if the resolved blocks directory is not an existing directory, INIT-ERROR with "Specified blocks directory \"%s\" does not exist." before anything is opened -- since a silently-created directory on the wrong volume is the failure this option is meant to prevent. Note that adding a defstruct slot to BLOCK-STORE needs the fresh-FASL cold lane (cl-workbench validation run cold-unit-fresh). A test should start a regtest node with -blocksdir into a second temp directory and assert blk00000.dat and xor.dat exist there and NOT under the datadir, with the reverse assertion as the positive control.
